title: Sentinel Ventures - Security & Deployment Constraints Discovery
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments
summary: Initial security posture discovery with Sentinel Ventures focused on compliance (SOC2/ISO), SSO/SCIM integration, fine-grained RBAC, audit/log retention, and encryption/KMS requirements. Customer leaning toward Dedicated for predictable throughput but needs Private/VPC for EU data residency and HSM support. Agreed next steps: send SOC2 and ISO artifacts, share KMS/HSM integration notes, schedule SE deep dive demo and whiteboard for network topology.
next_steps: Jordan to share SOC2 and ISO-27001 summary and redacted report (due 2027-12-10)
Maya to schedule technical deep dive for private deployment with Nora and Dante (week of 2027-12-13)
Customer to provide list of required retention windows and EU data residency constraint (Liam) by 2027-12-12
Jordan to provide pricing ballpark for Dedicated + optional Private deployment options
action_items: Jordan Park - send SOC2/ISO artifacts and compliance FAQ (due 2027-12-10)
Maya Singh - prepare private deployment network diagram and HSM/KMS integration notes (due 2027-12-12)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-08
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (CISO, Sentinel), Nora Patel (Senior SRE, Sentinel), Dante Ruiz (Head of Platform, Sentinel)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy):
- High level compliance questions about SOC2/ISO and audit logs.
- Strong interest in Dedicated for throughput; Private for EU residency and HSM.
- Questions on SAML/SCIM, RBAC hierarchy, and retention windows.

00:00 Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood inference team, this call's just to get a sense of Sentinel's constraints and what you folks need around security and deployment. Maya's gonna cover the technical bits after a quick intro.
00:12 Liam Ortiz: Hi Jordan, thanks. I'm Liam, CISO. Quick background, we handle payment orchestration and are subject to pci-ish controls, and we've got EU customers so data residency and encryption in transit and at rest are critical.
00:22 Nora Patel: Nora here, we run the platform, we care about latency SLAs, also SSO integration with our Okta is a must, and audit trails.
00:28 Dante Ruiz: Dante, head of platform. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. Main thing is predictable latency during peak batch windows and ability to key-manage with our HSM.
00:38 Jordan: Great, thanks. Quick run through agenda: compliance posture (SOC2, ISO), SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, RBAC and audit logs, encryption and KMS/HSM, data retention/residency, and deployment modes. Any additions?
00:47 Liam: No, that covers it.
00:50 Maya Singh: I'll jump into the technical questions as you go. One note — I might use shorthand like KV cache or prefix caching, say if that's ok — sometimes the auto-transcript mangles it.
00:58 Jordan: Fair. So Liam, first—are you required to run with a private VPC or is customer-managed KMS enough?
01:05 Liam: For some datasets we need to ensure keys are in our HSM; we cannot have keys managed by a third-party cloud KMS. So HSM-backed KMS is required for the EU-regulated buckets. For other workloads, customer-managed KMS in the cloud is acceptable.
01:18 Maya: Ok, so that's HSM in front of the key store. Redwood supports a few patterns: customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS or GCP KMS with BYOK, and for private deployments we can integrate with an on-prem HSM over a secure link. There's some setup around key wrapping and rotations.
01:32 Nora: Do you support FKMS or hardware tokens? I mean we use Nitro enclaves for some things, and we want double-wrapped keys.
01:40 Maya: We call out the double-wrap pattern in our ops docs — can do envelope encryption with customer master key in HSM, yes. For hosted we do rotation on schedule but customer retains CMKs in their account when configured as dedicated-private. Sometimes the transcript shows K-M-S as letters, but yes, KMS.
01:55 Dante: How about RBAC — we need least-privilege roles for ops vs data scientists vs engineers, and audit logs must be tamper-evident. Can you do field-level access and token scoping?
02:06 Jordan: We provide role-based access controls with token scoping. In Hosted, tokens can be scoped per route/model and we have audit trails. In Dedicated and Private deployments, you get stronger isolation and can plug in your SSO/SCIM and your audit storage.
02:20 Maya: To add, our RBAC supports hierarchical roles and scoped API keys. You can map Okta groups to roles via SCIM and SAML with SSO. The audit logs are shipped to an external logging endpoint — customers typically ship to Splunk/Elastic/Chronicle.
02:35 Nora: Is there an immutable log option or WORM storage for audits? We need tamper-resistance for 2 years.
02:42 Maya: For Dedicated and Private, yes — you can configure log export to append-only storage in your account or S3 buckets with Object Lock (WORM). Hosted customers can request long-term retention; we currently export logs to a retention system but for compliance we recommend Dedicated/Private.
02:57 Liam: SOC2 and ISO — do you have reports we can review? Also, do you support penetration test windows and shared responsibility documents?
03:06 Jordan: Yes, we maintain SOC2 Type II and ISO-27001 artifacts. I'll share a redacted report and a compliance FAQ after the call. We also have a shared responsibility matrix and annual pentest summaries.
03:17 Dante: Any issues with exchanging an NDA and letting you see more specifics?
03:20 Jordan: We can do an NDA if needed. Usually SOC2 bits are shared under an NDA.
03:25 Nora: SAML specifics — we use Okta and require Just-In-Time provisioning via SCIM with group mappings. We also use email 2FA and conditional access policies.
03:33 Maya: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and SCIM 2.0. We sync groups and can honor Okta conditional access through SAML assertions. There can be a small integration window to map group attributes.
03:45 Liam: How do you sign tokens and rotate them? We need to audit all token issuances.
03:50 Maya: API keys and tokens support rotation; we provide a token issuance log. For high-assurance tokens you can use short-lived JWTs issued by your identity provider; Redwood will accept those via SSO flows.
04:04 Jordan: Let's talk data residency — you mentioned EU. Do you need processing and storage in EU-only zones?
04:10 Liam: Yes, EU data must not leave EU region and keys must be in EU HSM. Some derived artifacts (embeddings) are considered PII for us so they must be stored per-region.
04:21 Maya: We offer region pinning for Dedicated and Private, and Hosted has regional deployment options — but for strict EU-only guarantees, Private or a Dedicated GPU cluster in an EU region pinned to the tenant is best.
04:33 Dante: If we go Dedicated in EU, can we still fall back to Hosted in emergencies? We need a failover plan but must avoid data egress.
04:40 Jordan: We can route fallback traffic to a compatible model in the same region if configured; automatic fallbacks to other regions are opt-in and disabled by default for customers with strict residency. That said, capacity constraints can complicate things.
04:54 Nora: What about model variants and quantization — will different variants produce different audit trails or be tracked differently?
05:00 Maya: Model variants are tagged and versioned; audit logs include model ID, variant, token counts, and latency metrics. If you use quantized variants, the runtime metadata still records the variant name so you'll have provenance.
05:12 Liam: Encryption at rest — does Redwood encrypt per-tenant with separate keys or is it a cluster-level key?
05:18 Maya: For Hosted default it's cluster-managed but we support per-tenant encryption via customer-managed keys in KMS when configured. Dedicated always supports per-tenant KMS. Private obviously fully under your control.
05:30 Dante: HSM integration — does Redwood integrate with on-prem HSMs over TLS? We need an approved FIPS 140-2/3 HSM.
05:38 Maya: Yes, for Private we can integrate with HSMs over a secure link; we also support connecting to AWS CloudHSM or Azure Dedicated HSM. We validate FIPS compliance with our security team and can provide attestations.
05:51 Liam: Audit log retention — default retention windows? We might need 24 months for some trails, 7 years for others.
05:58 Jordan: Hosted default is 90 days; Dedicated you can extend via log export to your storage. Private is customer-defined. The tradeoff is storage cost vs retrieval speed.
06:10 Nora: Ok, cost question — Dedicated looks good for throughput but how big is the footprint for our peak batch windows? We need predictability more than lowest cost.
06:19 Jordan: Dedicated is designed for predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools. We can give suggestions after we see your token per second distribution and sequence length. We can also set autoscale thresholds and burst configs.
06:31 Dante: Do you support canary rollouts and A/B deploys? We want gradual rollouts and automatic fallback if latency spikes.
06:37 Maya: Yes, rollouts with canary, A/B, and automated fallback policies are in the console. We'll demo that in the SE deep dive.
06:46 Liam: On legal/audit side, do you offer attestations for data deletion and retention? We have strict deletion windows for sandbox vs prod.
06:54 Jordan: We have deletion APIs and can provide deletion certificates for Private/Dedicated. Hosted can support deletion but for strict e-discovery you may want Dedicated/Private for stronger SLAs.
07:05 Nora: How about network egress — can we do VPC peering or private link?
07:10 Maya: For Dedicated and Private we do VPC peering and/or PrivateLink options; hosted supports PrivateLink in select regions. Data path diagrams will be included in the notes I send.
07:21 Dante: Any limits on encryption algorithms — we prefer AES-GCM and RSA-3072 or Ed25519 signatures.
07:27 Maya: We support AES-GCM for data at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit. Key types can be RSA or EC depending on KMS provider — HSM constraints apply but generally yes.
07:38 Jordan: Quick pause — any blockers that would immediately rule out Hosted vs Dedicated or Private?
07:43 Liam: HSM requirement for EU keys rules out pure Hosted unless you can guarantee BYOK with EU HSM. Also immutable audit WORM is a must.
07:52 Nora: Also need SCIM group sync and SSO with conditional access — if that's not possible it's a blocker.
07:58 Maya: Both are doable — SCIM, SAML, group mappings, and export to WORM storage are all supported, but Hosted may require additional contractual controls.
08:10 Jordan: Let's go through a short compliance checklist verbally — SOC2 Type II, ISO-27001, penetration testing, data residency, HSM/backed KMS, SAML+SCIM, audit log WORM, retention windows, and deletion certs.
08:24 Liam: We need those artifacts and a proposed architecture for EU private deployment.
08:29 Jordan: Agreed. I'll share SOC2/ISO redacted artifacts. Maya will prepare a EU private deployment topology with HSM and log export to your S3 with object lock. We'll also include SCIM mapping notes.
08:42 Dante: Can we schedule the SE deep dive next week? We want to invite engineering, infra, and their SRE.
08:47 Maya: I'm free Wed/Thu next week — I'll propose times via calendar invite after this call.
08:52 Jordan: For pricing — are you expecting a ballpark committed spend or are you still evaluating?
08:56 Dante: We need some numbers for Dedicated with EU region cluster and HSM integration, plus options for Private on-prem. Ballpark is fine.
09:04 Jordan: I'll put together a ballpark in the follow-up.
09:07 Nora: A couple of small technical Qs — do you keep KV cache warm on Dedicated after idle periods? We saw cold-start token latency in another provider.
09:16 Maya: Dedicated supports warm pools and continuous batching optimization. We can tune GC and keep KV cache warm based on traffic patterns.
09:25 Liam: Do you offer contractual SLAs for latency percentiles?
09:28 Jordan: Dedicated comes with SLA for uptime and we can include latency SLOs in enterprise contracts depending on commit levels. Hosted has standard SLAs but not the same latency guarantees.
09:40 Dante: How about audit for model outputs — we need traceability on requests that touched customer data vs public data.
09:47 Maya: We log request inputs/metadata (configurable redaction options). For strict use-cases, we recommend Private since you can control retention and storage.
09:55 Liam: Ok that's helpful. Any other questions from Sentinel?
09:58 Nora: Not right now.
10:00 Jordan: Ok, recap — action items: Jordan sends SOC2/ISO artifacts and compliance FAQ, Maya builds private-EU topology and HSM notes, Liam shares retention policy. We'll schedule SE deep dive. Anything to add?
10:14 Liam: Please redact sensitive IP from reports before sending.
10:18 Jordan: Of course. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by email and update CRM.
10:24 Meeting ends

Notes about transcription: There are small mislabels and filler words; speaker attribution is mostly correct. Some technical terms spelled out or hyphenated inconsistently (K M S, K-M-S, KV cache).
